patterns.use: One product object becomes the next (prompt node becomes image node). Keeps the eye on one subject across the handoff.
Hard cut between two subjects sharing silhouette or position; land the cut on a sound accent.
Move the world toward the next product detail instead of swapping panels. Stage is the world container.
The stage (world container) compensates for the subject's next position, arriving first, then holds perfectly still through the rest; ties consecutive beats into one continuous take instead of a cut.
Words arrive on the beat; with target set, the words collapse into the object they name.
Cursor travels, presses, product state changes. The proof action for software products.
Scattered parts converge into the finished surface. Offsets are fixed data, never random.
Wipe exposes the product inside the scene where it is used, not on an empty card.

patterns.audio: hits: the bar jumps to floor + (1 - floor) * strength on each hit and falls back to floor before the next
patterns.markup: .fk-meter > .fk-meter__track > .fk-meter__bar; the target is the bar (.fk-meter__bar); .fk-meter--x with axis x
patterns.use: A product level (queue load, throughput) that bounces on every hit. One lane on one bar; axis y rises from the bottom, x fills from the left.

patterns.audio: hits: each column is a meter lane fed the hits shifted by j * travel / N and scaled by decay^j, so a pulse travels across the row; events, not a waveform
patterns.markup: .fk-scope > .fk-scope__col x N; columns lists one selector per column (.fk-scope__col)
patterns.productRole: activity or heartbeat of a process
patterns.use: A process trace whose pulses travel across thin bars. Pass one selector per column so every column has its own lane.

patterns.audio: hits: one row scrolls in per hit, a step of at most step seconds, truncated at the next hit; throws when hits exceed rows
patterns.markup: .fk-log > .fk-log__col > .fk-log__row x M; the target is the column (.fk-log__col); rowPx equals the log row height custom property
patterns.use: A log or feed that gains one line per hit. The column steps up by rowPx and stays; the frame clips it.

patterns.audio: hits: per hit the perHit share of cells with the lowest hash(seed + hitIndex, cellIndex) light up and release; one lane per cell; strength is not used
patterns.markup: .fk-cells > .fk-cell x N; cells lists one selector per cell (.fk-cell)
patterns.use: A matrix of jobs, nodes or cells that light on the beat. rest and lit are literal colours from the STYLE table, never var().

patterns.audio: hits (optional): every hit bites a share off the timer; the value is the static text times one minus the share burned; zero from until - freeze, then a no-op hold
patterns.markup: .fk-readout--display > .fk-readout__value; the static text is the start value written the way format writes it (08.00)
patterns.use: A timer that accelerates toward the drop. One to tween on innerText with a modifiers formatter; there is no start option, GSAP reads the start from the markup. textColor and alert are literals given together.

patterns.audio: a cue time: flash of one frame, zoom punch and a shake of one-frame steps at the hit; the caller keeps other instruments still in [hit - freeze, hit) with the adapter quiet option
patterns.markup: .fk-flash (full-bleed overlay) and .fk-stage (a wrapper no camera pattern drives in the same window)
patterns.productRole: the moment the product ships or completes
patterns.use: The drop: an overlay flash, a zoom punch and a shake at the cue; returns hit + 0.4. With zoom 1 and shakeFrames 0 it is a flash-only accent, which makes a hard cut visible to the scene detector.

helpers.grid: lib/score-grid.js calls FilmAudio.setGrid(<score-grid.json>); load it after audio-events.js
helpers.use: Turns a score grid (film score) or an edit-analysis music block into plain data: hits() returns [{ atSec, strength }] for the instruments, beats() beat times, bar(audio, k) the window of bar k (1-based). Not a pattern; it reads the grid so the patterns never do. It throws, naming designer-pipeline film score, when no grid was set.

chrome.use: Neutral chrome for the instruments: monochrome defaults, no shipped font or image. A film overrides every slot from one STYLE table applied with document.documentElement.style.setProperty("--fk-" + key, value) and passes the same literals to the kit calls. A section re-scopes the slots on its own element.

properties.name: --fk-cols
properties.role: columns of a cell grid, per instance
